text: ACTIVITY CORNER AND OUR ORGANISATIONS TAKE THE SHAPES THE DESIGN DRAWS. Activity Corner was two columns showing events and photographs at once, under the heading "Events and Media". It is now three tabs over the three registers the design and the live page both name — Events, Press Releases, Circulars — each row a date block beside its title. The registers it shows are not the two it showed: the photographs are one click away under Events & Gallery, and the circulars, 164 of them and the register a citizen most often comes here for, were not on the home page at all. Our Organisations was three stacked groups with every body on screen at once; it is now two columns, what they are on the left and on the right the categories as chips carrying counts derived from the registry, with the cards of whichever is chosen. TWO THINGS THE DESIGN DRAWS THAT ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT. No description under an Activity card: not one of the three registers publishes one — an event carries a title, a date, a venue and a mode; a press item a title, a date and a picture; a circular a title, a date and a file — and a sentence we wrote about a document we have not read is not something a government page may carry. And no four bullets in the Organisations column: "Promotes equality and social participation for all communities" and its three neighbours are not the Department's words and trace to nothing it has published. The chips are the registry's three categories rather than the design's four; Figma splits the foundations into "Training & Capacity Building" (one body) and "Foundation & Autonomous Bodies" (three), and the registry holds five in one category — splitting it is a registry change every organisation page would inherit, not a home-page decision.
